summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a history of HCV and alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatic encephalopathy, and major depression was admitted due to altered mental status and difficulty standing, as noticed by her daughter. The confusion was multifactorial, stemming from noncompliance with lactulose, recent alcohol use, and accidental overdose of psychiatric medications, particularly taking double doses of Wellbutrin and excess Seroquel. She was treated with lactulose, vitamin supplementation, and benzodiazepines for alcohol withdrawal symptoms, while all sedating and anticholinergic medications were held. Her mental status improved over several days, and she was restarted on a simplified regimen of bupropion and trazodone per psychiatry. Labs showed stable thrombocytopenia and leukopenia, and imaging revealed cirrhotic changes without acute findings. She was discharged home with services, new supplements for alcohol-related deficiencies, and plans for outpatient follow-up in psychiatry, hepatology, and a geriatric day program for ongoing support.
